name: Luna 10
short_status: Entered lunar orbit 3 Apr 1966, the first artificial satellite of another world; 460 orbits and 219 radio sessions before batteries died 30 May 1966; later crashed at an unknown date and place.
tagline: Soviet Union · Orbiter · 1966 · The space race Success
stats: artificial satellite of the Moon (or any world beyond Earth)
radio sessions in 56 days of operation
orbital period, 350 x 1,017 km at 71.9 degrees

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 31 March 1966, 10:46:59 UT (13:46:59 Moscow), Molniya-M from Baikonur, via an Earth-orbit parking platform

facts.label: Spacecraft
facts.value: E-6S (No. 210), an E-6 landing bus modified to carry a detachable sealed instrument satellite of 248.5 kg (about 245 kg in some NASA sources); launch mass about 1,584 kg; no camera aboard

facts.label: Lunar orbit insertion
facts.value: 3 April 1966, 18:44 UT: 57-second braking burn; the satellite separated at 18:45:39 UT

facts.label: Initial orbit
facts.value: 350 x 1,017 km, inclination 71.9 degrees, period about 2 h 58 min

facts.label: Instruments
facts.value: Gamma-ray spectrometer (0.3-3.0 MeV NaI(Tl)), triaxial magnetometer, micrometeorite detectors, charged-particle traps, gas-discharge counters, infrared detector, X-ray photon counters

facts.label: The Internationale
facts.value: Played to the 23rd Party Congress on 4 April 1966 at 10:00 Moscow time; after an oscillator dropped a note in the morning test, controllers routed the previous night's rehearsal recording to the hall, a secret for about 30 years

facts.label: Sister craft
facts.value: The first E-6S (No. 204) launched 1 March 1966, was stranded in Earth orbit by an attitude-control failure as Kosmos 111, and reentered 3 March 1966

facts.label: Operations
facts.value: 460 lunar orbits and 219 radio sessions over 56 days; battery-powered, last contact 30 May 1966

facts.label: Fate
facts.value: Orbit eventually decayed; Luna 10 crashed on the Moon at an unknown date and location, so there is no landing-site pin

timeline: Luna 9's landing frees the E-6 bus for a rush conversion to a lunar orbiter, targeting the Party Congress opening in late March
First E-6S attempt fails in Earth orbit as Kosmos 111; it reenters two days later
The 23rd Congress of the Communist Party opens in Moscow, the political deadline driving the schedule
Luna 10 launches at 10:47 UT from Baikonur on a Molniya-M
18:44 UT: 57-second braking burn: the first spacecraft ever to orbit another world; the 248.5 kg satellite separates at 18:45:39 UT
The Internationale rings through the Kremlin Palace of Congresses, presented as live from lunar orbit but actually the overnight rehearsal tape
Batteries exhausted after 460 orbits and 219 radio sessions; radio contact ends
NASA's Lunar Orbiter 1 becomes the first US spacecraft to orbit the Moon, four and a half months later
Luna 10's orbit decays and it strikes the Moon at an undetermined location
